title: Annotatio II NATIVITAS: Cuno of Siegburg — accomplice and patron of Rupert’s sentence
pass_a_gloss: He also got CUNO Abbot of Siegburg as accomplice and favorer of his sentence — of whom, in the preface prefixed to his books On the works of the Trinity on Genesis and Exodus, he writes among other things that CUNO alone, nay through Cuno (as he says) Christ was present to him as a guard against those who were troublesome to this work and who both by words and deeds roared against him — as if Cuno had been made a peg for him, set in a faithful place, on which he might hang the vessel of his hope.
pass_b_english: Rupert names Cuno, Abbot of Siegburg, accomplice and patron of his sentence.
In the Genesis/Exodus preface Christ stood by him through Cuno alone against those who roared at the work — Cuno a peg in a faithful place for the vessel of his hope.
source_text: CUNONEM etiam Abbatem Sigebergensem, complicem & fautorem sententiae suae nactum, utpote de quo, in praefatione, libris suis, de operibus Trinitatis in Genesin & Exodum, praefixa, inter alia scribit, quòd solus CUNO, imò per Cunonem, (ut ait) Christus praesidio sibi adfuit contra eos, qui molesti fuere huic operi, & qui tùm dictis tùm factis, fremuerunt in ipsum, quasi paxillus sibi Cuno factus sit, positus in loco fideli, in quo spei suae possit vasculum suspendi.
